name: Calcific Uremic Arteriolopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Histopathological evidence of medial calcification of small and medium-sized arterioles
Presence of painful, necrotic skin ulcers or plaques typically on adipose-rich areas
Underlying end-stage renal disease or severe chronic kidney disease
Exclusion of other causes of skin necrosis such as vasculitis or infection

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic skin lesions with histopathological confirmation of vascular calcification
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires skin biopsy; clinical suspicion is critical in patients with renal failure

pathognomonic.notes: Typically occurs in areas with high adipose tissue such as thighs and abdomen

common.symptomName: Severe localized pain at lesion sites

laboratory: Elevated serum phosphate and calcium-phosphate product
imaging: Bone scintigraphy demonstrating soft tissue calcification
Ultrasound or CT showing calcified vessels
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; associated with metabolic derangements
other: Skin biopsy showing medial calcification of arterioles with intimal proliferation and thrombosis

distinguishingFeatures: Onset shortly after initiation of anticoagulation
Presence of protein C or S deficiency
Systemic symptoms such as fever and malaise
Histopathology showing inflammatory infiltrates rather than calcification

redFlags: Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
Underlying end-stage renal disease with metabolic abnormalities
references: Nigwekar SU, et al. Calciphylaxis: Risk factors, diagnosis, and treatment. Am J Kidney Dis. 2015.
Weenig RH. Calciphylaxis: An overview. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2008.
Fine A, Zacharias J. Calciphylaxis is usually non-ulcerating: Risk factors, outcome and therapy. Kidney Int. 2002.
